# Results -- Study 257 (AAII-Sentiment) on real monthly tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Recipe: join the
curated monthly AAII bull-bear table to ^GSPC month-end closes; at each month-end
*t*, the observed bull-bear spread predicts the S&P **price** return earned during
month *t+1* (one-month execution lag). The contrarian claim: low (panicked)
sentiment -> higher next-month return; high (euphoric) sentiment -> lower.
**Sentiment is a curated, revised monthly snapshot, not the point-in-time weekly
tape** -- all results are upper bounds on the live edge. As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Shape | Fingerprint (spread) |
|--------|--------|-------|----------------------|
| AAII curated monthly + ^GSPC month-end (price-only) | 1987-08 -> 2026-05 | 182 months | `714da328c0fd` |

## Primary specification (next-month price return by prior sentiment tercile)

| Regime (prior spread) | Next-month return | HAC *t* | n |
|-----------------------|-------------------|---------|---|
| **Low (panic)** | **+23.8%/yr** | **+2.24** | 61 |
| Mid | +4.8%/yr | +0.62 | 55 |
| High (euphoria) | +8.5%/yr | +1.78 | 66 |
| **Low - High gap** | **+15.3 pp/yr** | -- | -- |

- The **direction is the contrarian one**: panicked months are followed by much
  stronger returns than euphoric months.
- But only the **low** regime nears significance (*t* = +2.24); **euphoria is not
  a reliable sell** -- high-sentiment months still average a *positive* return.

## Headline tests -- the contrarian edge is WEAK

| Test | Estimate | HAC *t* |
|------|----------|---------|
| Long-short (long panic / short euphoria) | +0.59%/mo on active months | **+1.18** |
| Predictive regression slope (ret ~ std. spread) | **-0.66%/sd** | **-1.54** |
| Regression R-squared | ~1.8% | -- |

The regression **slope sign is correct (negative = contrarian)** but **|t| < 2**,
and the R-squared is ~2% -- sentiment explains almost none of next-month variance.
By the desk rubric (REAL needs HAC *t* >= 2 on the real tape), this is **WEAK**.

## Tradability -- the overlay LOSES to buy-and-hold

| Strategy (price-only, 5 bps one-way) | Return | Ann. Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|--------------------------------------|--------|-------------|---------|
| Long/flat contrarian overlay (sit out euphoria) | **+9.3%/yr** | +0.6 | +2.23 |
| **Buy-and-hold ^GSPC (price-only)** | **+12.5%/yr** | -- | -- |

Net of trivial costs the overlay returns **less** than simply staying invested:
high sentiment coincides with the meat of bull markets you cannot afford to skip.
The contrarian "edge" is concentrated in a few violent rebounds (2009, 2020)
visible only with hindsight.

## Sub-period analysis -- direction stable, significance not

| Period | Low regime | High regime | Low *t* | n |
|--------|-----------|-------------|---------|---|
| 1987-1999 | +21.3%/yr | +15.5%/yr | +1.07 | 55 |
| 2000-2012 | +18.7%/yr | +3.2%/yr | +0.80 | 62 |
| 2013-2026 | +33.8%/yr | +7.8%/yr | +2.26 | 65 |

Low > high in **every** sub-period (robust direction), but the low-regime t-stat
clears 2 only in the most recent slice -- and on a curated, revised snapshot.

## Positive control -- the machinery finds a contrarian edge when planted

On the deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_monthly`) the predictive
regression recovers the planted contrarian loading and reads ~zero on the null:

| Planted edge | Regression slope HAC *t* |
|-------------|--------------------------|
| 0.00 (null) | **-0.20** (~0) |
| +0.06       | **-2.99** (significant negative) |

The engine works; the real tape simply carries a weak, untradeable version.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- WEAK.** The contrarian *direction* is real and stable across all
  sub-periods (panic +23.8%/yr vs euphoria +8.5%/yr), but the headline long-short
  HAC *t* = +1.18 and the predictive-regression slope *t* = -1.54 both fall short
  of the *t* >= 2 bar; R-squared ~2%. Literature (Fisher-Statman 2000) supports
  the sign but not a robust, tradable magnitude. The sentiment series is a curated,
  revised monthly snapshot (not point-in-time weekly), so even this is an upper
  bound. Verdict: **WEAK**.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** A long/flat contrarian overlay nets **+9.3%/yr**,
  *below* buy-and-hold's **+12.5%/yr**: sitting out euphoria skips the core of
  bull markets. The edge lives in a handful of ex-post-obvious rebounds and never
  pays for the missed upside. Verdict: **MIRAGE**.
- **Vintage / survivorship -- named.** Curated monthly snapshot; the live weekly
  edge a real trader could have captured is weaker still.
